input.summary:
P0 parlour lights are NOT in build.nbt: room-2.mjs build() is still commented out and shell-west fills the parlour interior with air, which runParts locks, so the designed lanterns, candle and lamp cannot land yet.
Scratch copy of build.nbt (in /tmp/lamp-sim, real build.nbt untouched) with the designer's full layout and four lights: min 10, mean 11.9, 0 dark, 0 dim, all 19 reachable cells lit. That matches the designer's scratch result.
Nothing in the workdir changed, and make.sh was not re-run because there was nothing new to build.
left: parts/room-2.mjs build() is still empty: uncomment layers(g, [3, 2, 14], LEGEND, LAYOUT) once shell-west leaves the parlour interior (x3..12, z14..20, y2..top) as open space instead of locked air. Until then the parlour has no furniture and none of its four lights (3,4,15), (4,4,19), (4,4,17) candle, (3,3,20) in build.nbt.

The lock is shell-west's air fill (parts/shell-west.mjs lines 15-16) plus runParts' lock; it is not the lamplighter's to change. Not re-run through the guarded build: the refusal is taken from the designer's recorded 28 of 28 refused and the runParts docs.

Current real build.nbt parlour (empty room): min 7, 2 dim cells, 0 dark. The tool's suggested lantern at (3,2,16) is for the empty room only; re-measure after the furniture lands rather than adding it now.

After the lock is fixed, re-run ./make.sh and `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "P0 parlour"` to confirm min >= 8 with the furniture actually placed (the scratch run has the furniture; the real one is what counts).

waste.what: To check the designer's four lights I copied the parlour's LEGEND and LAYOUT by hand into a scratch script, then placed the lights over build.nbt and re-measured.
waste.cost: 2 tool calls, one scratch script of about 30 lines, and a manual check that the four target cells were air.
waste.tool: A room command such as `mcd room --simulate parts/room-2.mjs` that runs the module's drawing onto a copy and reports the light map plus the cells runParts would refuse, without a full make. Or export LEGEND and LAYOUT from the room module so they can be reused.

waste.what: The parts report shows 'room: P0 parlour' as placed 0, refused 0, so the lock problem is invisible. The designer had to measure the 28 refusals by hand.
waste.cost: No tool call; the gap only surfaced after reading shell-west and the runParts docs.
waste.tool: runParts should report the cells a commented-out or inactive room drawing would have written and had refused, so a locked interior shows up in parts-report.json.

companions.task: Uncomment room-2's build() call once the shell leaves the parlour interior open, then confirm the furniture and lights land and re-measure the light map.
Stop filling the parlour interior (x3..12, z14..20) with air, or hand that interior to the room part, so runParts' lock doesn't refuse the room's cells.
